correctness.summary: The CG-Lanczos tridiagonal has an LDL^T factorization whose unit-lower-bidiagonal multipliers are the adjacent residual ratios. Every trailing Schur complement remains spectrally enclosed in [mu,L] because its inverse is a principal block of the inverse Lanczos matrix. A sharp two-by-two spectral-interval lemma then gives each multiplier at most (L-mu)/(2 sqrt(L mu)). A two-dimensional endpoint-spectrum construction attains equality, and deterministic numerical checks reproduce the formulas.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Bouyouli, Meurant, Smoch, and Sadok (2009) give the directly comparable all-step bound ||r_k||/||r_{k-1}|| <= (kappa-1)/2. The present result sharpens it by a factor sqrt(kappa) and proves the improved constant globally sharp. Meurant (2020) contains a two-dimensional feasibility discriminant that is equivalent to the sharp first-step endpoint-spectrum frontier, so the first-step constant itself is not claimed as new. Searches across residual-increase terminology, CG beta coefficients, Lanczos/LDL formulations, condition-number bounds, and recent CG surveys did not locate the same sharp all-step theorem, exact universal monotonicity threshold, or fixed-SPD-preconditioned M^{-1}-residual extension. Older Lanczos/CG monographs and elimination-factor literature remain a material historical-equivalence risk.

value.summary: The theorem turns a known condition-number residual-growth estimate into an exact frontier, identifies the precise kappa = 3 + 2 sqrt(2) boundary for universal stepwise residual monotonicity, yields a one-step lower certificate on conditioning from an exact-arithmetic residual spike, and transfers cleanly to the natural residual norm for fixed SPD preconditioning.

limitations: Exact arithmetic only; no statement is made about finite-precision residual gaps or attainable accuracy.
Real finite-dimensional SPD systems and standard CG only.
The sharp constant uses the actual global spectral condition number; enclosing spectral estimates may be conservative.
For fixed SPD preconditioning, the extension concerns the M^{-1} residual norm rather than ordinary Euclidean residual norm in general.
Global sharpness is witnessed at the first iteration; equality at arbitrary prescribed later iterations is not claimed.
The theorem is a worst-case adjacent-step bound, not an iteration-count estimate and not a substitute for spectrum-distribution-dependent CG analysis.
Older Lanczos/CG and Gaussian-elimination/Cholesky multiplier literature was not exhaustively inspected theorem by theorem, leaving residual originality uncertainty.
Independent audit has not been performed.
